paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文字。为每个编号的空白处选择最佳的单词，并在答题卡上标记 A、B、C 或 D。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Why do people read negative Internet comments and do other things that will obviously be painful? Because humans have an inherent need to 1 uncertainty, according to a recent study in Psychological Science. The new research reveals that the need to know is so strong that people will 2 to satisfy their curiosity even when it is clear the answer will 3 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么人们会阅读负面的网络评论并做其他明显会痛苦的事情？根据《心理科学》最近的一项研究，因为人类有解决不确定性的内在需求。新的研究表明，求知欲是如此强烈，以至于人们会寻求满足自己的好奇心，即使答案显然会带来伤害。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a series of four experiments, behavioral scientists at the University of Chicago and the Wisconsin School of Business tested students’ willingness to 4 themselves to unpleasant stimuli in an effort to satisfy curiosity. For one 5 , each participant was shown a pile of pens that the researcher claimed were from a previous experiment. The twist? Half of the pens would 6 an electric shock when clicked.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一系列四项实验中，芝加哥大学和威斯康星商学院的行为科学家测试了学生为了满足好奇心而暴露在不愉快刺激下的意愿。在一次试验中，每个参与者都看到了一堆钢笔，研究人员声称这些钢笔来自之前的实验。转折？一半的笔在点击时会产生电击。

paragraphs.sourceText: Twenty-seven students were told which pens were electrified; another twenty-seven were told only that some were electrified. 7 left alone in the room, the students who did not know which ones would shock them clicked more pens and incurred more shocks than the students who knew what would 8 . Subsequent experiments reproduced this effect with other stimuli, 9 the sound of fingernails on a chalkboard and photographs of disgusting insects.
paragraphs.translationZh: 二十七名学生被告知哪些笔是带电的；另外二十七人只被告知其中一些人触电了。当单独留在房间里时，那些不知道哪些会电击他们的学生比那些知道会发生什么的学生敲击的笔更多，受到的电击也更多。随后的实验用其他刺激重现了这种效果，例如指甲敲黑板的声音和令人厌恶的昆虫的照片。

paragraphs.sourceText: The drive to 10 is deeply rooted in humans, much the same as the basic drives for 11 or shelter, says Christopher Hsee of the University of Chicago. Curiosity is often considered a good instinct — it can 12 new scientific advances, for instance — but sometimes such 13 can backfire. The insight that curiosity can drive you to do 14 things is a profound one.
paragraphs.translationZh: 芝加哥大学的克里斯托弗·赫西 (Christopher Hsee) 表示，探索的动力深深植根于人类之中，与寻求食物或住所的基本动力非常相似。好奇心通常被认为是一种良好的本能——例如，它可以带来新的科学进步——但有时这种探究可能会适得其反。好奇心会驱使你做出自我毁灭的事情，这一点是深刻的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unhealthy curiosity is possible to 15 , however. In a final experiment, participants who were encouraged to 16 how they would feel after viewing an unpleasant picture were less likely to 17 to see such an image. These results suggest that imagining the 18 of following through on one’s curiosity ahead of time can help determine 19 it is worth the endeavor. “Thinking about long-term 20 is key to reducing the possible negative effects of curiosity,” Hsee says. In other words, don’t read online comments.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，不健康的好奇心是可以抵制的。在最后的实验中，被鼓励预测自己在观看不愉快的图片后的感受的参与者不太可能选择看到这样的图像。这些结果表明，提前想象一下满足好奇心的结果可以帮助确定是否值得付出努力。 “考虑长期后果是减少好奇心可能带来的负面影响的关键，”Hsee 说。换句话说，不要阅读网上评论。

paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读下面四篇课文。选择 A、B、C 或 D 来回答每篇课文后的问题。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （40分）

paragraphs.sourceText: It is curious that Stephen Koziatek feels almost as though he has to justify his efforts to give his students a better future.
paragraphs.translationZh: 奇怪的是，史蒂芬·科齐亚泰克似乎觉得他必须证明自己为给学生一个更好的未来所做的努力是合理的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Mr. Koziatek is part of something pioneering. He is a teacher at a New Hampshire high school where learning is not something of books and tests and mechanical memorization, but practical. When did it become accepted wisdom that students should be able to name the 13th president of the United States but be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain?
paragraphs.translationZh: Koziatek 先生是开创性事业的一部分。他是新罕布什尔州一所高中的老师，那里的学习不是书本、考试和机械记忆，而是实践。学生们应该能够说出美国第 13 任总统的名字，但却被断掉的自行车链条彻底压倒，这从什么时候开始成为公认的智慧？

paragraphs.sourceText: As Koziatek knows, there is learning in just about everything. Nothing is necessarily gained by forcing students to learn geometry at a graffitied desk stuck with generations of discarded chewing gum. They can also learn geometry by assembling a bicycle.
paragraphs.translationZh: 正如 Koziatek 所知，几乎所有事情都需要学习。强迫学生在一张贴满了几代人丢弃的口香糖的涂鸦桌子上学习几何，不一定会得到任何好处。他们还可以通过组装自行车来学习几何。

paragraphs.sourceText: But he’s also found a kind of insidious prejudice. Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority. Schools in the family of vocational education “have that stereotype…that it’s for kids who can’t make it academically,” he says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但他也发现了一种阴险的偏见。用手工作几乎被视为自卑的标志。他说，职业教育大家庭中的学校“有一种刻板印象……这是为那些学业成绩不佳的孩子准备的”。

paragraphs.sourceText: On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America’s evolution. Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was. The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated. More education is the new principle. We want more for our kids, and rightfully so.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一方面，这种观点是美国发展的逻辑产物。制造业不再像以前那样是经济引擎。美国经济曾经为高中毕业生提供的就业保障已基本消失。加强教育是新原则。我们希望为我们的孩子提供更多，这是理所当然的。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the headlong push into bachelor’s degrees for all — and the subtle devaluing of anything less — misses an important point: That’s not the only thing the American economy needs. Yes, a bachelor’s degree opens more doors. But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing. But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但一味地推动所有人获得学士学位——以及其他任何东西的微妙贬值——忽略了重要的一点：这并不是美国经济唯一需要的东西。是的，学士学位打开了更多的大门。但即便如此，该国 54% 的工作岗位仍属于中等技能岗位，例如建筑业和高技能制造业。但只有 44% 的工人接受过充分培训。

paragraphs.sourceText: In other words, at a time when the working class has turned the country on its political head, frustrated that the opportunity that once defined America is vanishing, one obvious solution is staring us in the face. There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren’t equipped to do them. Koziatek’s Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap.
paragraphs.translationZh: 换句话说，当工人阶级在政治上颠覆国家，对曾经定义美国的机会正在消失感到沮丧时，一个显而易见的解决方案就摆在我们面前。工人阶级的工作存在缺口，但最需要这些工作的工人却没有能力胜任这些工作。 Koziatek 的曼彻斯特理工学院高中正在努力填补这一空白。

paragraphs.sourceText: Koziatek’s school is a wake-up call. When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation’s diversity of gifts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科齐亚泰克的学校给我们敲响了警钟。当教育变得一刀切时，它就有可能忽视一个国家天赋的多样性。

paragraphs.sourceText: While fossil fuels — coal, oil, gas — still generate roughly 85 percent of the world’s energy supply, it’s clearer than ever that the future belongs to renewable sources such as wind and solar. The move to renewables is picking up momentum around the world: They now account for more than half of new power sources going on line.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管煤炭、石油、天然气等化石燃料仍占世界能源供应的约 85%，但比以往任何时候都更加清楚的是，未来属于风能和太阳能等可再生能源。全球范围内向可再生能源转型的势头正在增强：目前，可再生能源占新增发电电源的一半以上。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some growth stems from a commitment by governments and farsighted businesses to fund cleaner energy sources. But increasingly the story is about the plummeting prices of renewables, especially wind and solar. The cost of solar panels has dropped by 80 percent and the cost of wind turbines by close to one-third in the past eight years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些增长源于政府和有远见的企业为清洁能源提供资金的承诺。但越来越多的故事是关于可再生能源价格暴跌的，尤其是风能和太阳能。过去八年里，太阳能电池板的成本下降了 80%，风力涡轮机的成本下降了近三分之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: In many parts of the world renewable energy is already a principal energy source. In Scotland, for example, wind turbines provide enough electricity to power 95 percent of homes. While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe, the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift. In March, for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent of the power generated in the US, reported the US Energy Information Administration.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在世界许多地方，可再生能源已经成为主要能源。例如，在苏格兰，风力涡轮机提供的电力足以为 95% 的家庭供电。尽管世界其他地区（尤其是中国和欧洲）处于领先地位，但美国也出现了显着的转变。据美国能源情报署报告，3月份风能和太阳能发电量首次占美国发电量的10%以上。

paragraphs.sourceText: President Trump has underlined fossil fuels — especially coal — as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state’s electricity generation — and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 特朗普总统强调化石燃料——尤其是煤炭——是经济增长的途径。最近在爱荷华州的一次演讲中，他认为风力发电是一种不可靠的能源。但这一信息在爱荷华州的许多人中并不受欢迎，风力涡轮机遍布该州的田野，提供了该州 36% 的发电量，而且像微软这样的科技巨头也被清洁能源为其数据中心供电所吸引。

paragraphs.sourceText: The question “what happens when the wind doesn’t blow or the sun doesn’t shine?” has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely.
paragraphs.translationZh: “当风不吹或阳光不照时会发生什么？”这个问题。很快就让怀疑者失望了。但电池存储容量的提高使得它们更有可能保持全天候供电。

paragraphs.sourceText: The advance is driven in part by vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles. Although electric cars are still a rarity on roads now, this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一进步在一定程度上是由汽车制造商推动的，他们在电池驱动的电动汽车上下了很大的赌注。尽管电动汽车现在在道路上仍然很少见，但这项巨额投资可能会在未来几年迅速改变这一状况。

paragraphs.sourceText: While there’s a long way to go, the trend lines for renewables are spiking. The pace of change in energy sources appears to be speeding up — perhaps just in time to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change. What Washington does — or doesn’t do — to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管还有很长的路要走，但可再生能源的趋势线正在飙升。能源变化的步伐似乎正在加快——也许正好对减缓气候变化产生有意义的影响。在全球思想转变之际，华盛顿在推广替代能源方面所做的或没有做的事情可能意义越来越小。

paragraphs.sourceText: The power and ambition of the giants of the digital economy is astonishing — Amazon has just announced the purchase of the upmarket grocery chain Whole Foods for $13.5bn, but two years ago Facebook paid even more than that to acquire the WhatsApp messaging service, which doesn’t have any physical product at all. What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users’ friendships and social lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 数字经济巨头的力量和野心令人震惊——亚马逊刚刚宣布以 135 亿美元收购高档杂货连锁店 Whole Foods，但两年前 Facebook 斥资甚至更高的价格收购了根本没有任何实体产品的 WhatsApp 消息服务。 WhatsApp 为 Facebook 提供的是一个复杂而细致的网络，记录了用户的友谊和社交生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link phone numbers to Facebook identities, but it broke the promise almost as soon as the deal went through. Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be. What political journalist, what party whip, would not want to know the makeup of the WhatsApp groups in which Theresa May’s enemies are currently plotting? It may be that the value of Whole Foods to Amazon is not so much the 460 shops it owns, but the records of which customers have purchased what.
paragraphs.translationZh: Facebook 当时向欧盟委员会承诺，不会将电话号码与 Facebook 身份关联起来，但交易一完成，它就违背了承诺。即使不知道消息中的内容，了解消息的发送者和收件人也具有很大的启发性，而且仍然可能具有启发性。哪个政治记者、哪个党鞭不想知道特蕾莎·梅的敌人目前正在密谋的 WhatsApp 群组的构成？ Whole Foods 对亚马逊的价值可能不在于它拥有的 460 家商店，而在于哪些顾客购买了什么商品的记录。

paragraphs.sourceText: Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power. But it is clumsy. For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy. By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power. But there is a deeper conceptual problem, too. Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don’t pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers. That would be the people who buy advertising from them — and Facebook and Google, the two virtual giants, dominate digital advertising to the disadvantage of all other media and entertainment companies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 竞争法似乎是解决这些权力失衡的唯一途径。但它很笨拙。一方面，与数字经济的变化速度相比，它非常缓慢。当问题得到解决和补救时，它可能已经在市场上消失，取而代之的是新的权力滥用。但还有一个更深层次的概念问题。目前解释的竞争法涉及消费者的经济劣势，而当这些服务的用户不付费时，这一点并不明显。他们的服务的用户不是他们的客户。那将是那些从他们那里购买广告的人——而 Facebook 和谷歌这两个虚拟巨头主导着数字广告，这对所有其他媒体和娱乐公司来说都是不利的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The product they’re selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to date for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield. Ants keep predatory insects away from where their aphids feed; Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes. It doesn’t feel like a human or democratic relationship, even if both sides benefit.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们销售的产品是数据，而我们，用户，为了数字巨头的利益而改变我们的生活。正如一些蚂蚁养殖蚜虫是为了获取它们进食时产生的蜜露一样，谷歌养殖我们是为了我们的数字生活产生的数据。蚂蚁让捕食性昆虫远离蚜虫的食物来源； Gmail 将垃圾邮件发送者拒之门外。即使双方都受益，这也不像是一种人性或民主的关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of “deep work” — the ability to focus without distraction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了克服过于注重忙碌的陷阱，《深度工作：分心世界中专注成功的规则》一书的作者卡尔·纽波特建议养成“深度工作”的习惯，即不分心地专注的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work — be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a “journalistic” approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day. Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 掌握深度工作艺术的方法有很多种——可以是专门针对特定任务的长时间静修；也可以是长期静修。制定日常仪式；或者采取“新闻”的方式，抓住一天中可以进行深度工作的时刻。无论哪种方法，关键是确定你的专注时间长度并坚持下去。

paragraphs.sourceText: Newport also recommends “deep scheduling” to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time. “At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month. Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor’s appointment or important meeting,” he writes.
paragraphs.translationZh: 纽波特还建议“深度调度”，以应对持续的干扰，并在更短的时间内完成更多工作。 “在任何特定的时间点，我都应该在大约下个月安排深度工作。一旦列入日历，我就会像对待医生的预约或重要会议一样保护这段时间，”他写道。

paragraphs.sourceText: Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritize your day — in particular how we craft our to-do lists. Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在更短的时间内完成更多工作的另一种方法是重新思考如何确定一天的优先顺序，特别是我们如何制定待办事项列表。 《凌乱：改变我们生活的混乱的力量》一书的作者蒂姆·哈福德指出，20世纪80年代初的一项研究将本科生分为两组：一些人被建议制定每月目标和学习活动；另一些人被建议制定每月目标和学习活动；另一些人被建议制定每月目标和学习活动；另一些人被建议制定每月目标和学习活动。其他人则被告知要日复一日地更详细地计划活动和目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students. Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然研究人员认为结构良好的每日计划在执行任务时最有效，但他们错了：详细的每日计划会降低学生的积极性。哈福德认为，不可避免的干扰往往会使每日待办事项清单变得无效，而在这样的清单中留出即兴发挥的空间才能获得最佳结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, “be lazy.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了充分利用我们的注意力和精力，我们还需要接受休息时间，或者正如纽波特建议的那样，“变得懒惰”。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body… [idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done,” he argues.
paragraphs.translationZh: “无所事事不仅仅是一种度假、一种放纵或一种恶习；它对于大脑来说就像维生素 D 对于身体一样不可或缺……矛盾的是，[无所事事]却是完成任何工作所必需的，”他辩称。

paragraphs.sourceText: Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate. When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.
paragraphs.translationZh: 哈佛医学院精神病学助理教授斯里尼·皮莱 (Srini Pillay) 认为，停机时间和生产力之间这种违反直觉的联系可能是由于我们大脑的运作方式造成的。当我们的大脑在专注和不专注于某项任务之间切换时，它们往往会更有效率。

paragraphs.sourceText: “What people don’t realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain,” says Pillay.
paragraphs.translationZh: “人们没有意识到，为了完成这些任务，他们需要同时使用大脑中的聚焦和散焦回路，”皮莱说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Five Ways to Make Conversation with Anyone
paragraphs.translationZh: 与任何人交谈的五种方法

paragraphs.sourceText: Conversations are links, which means when you have a conversation with a new person a link gets formed and every conversation you have after that moment will strengthen the link.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对话就是链接，这意味着当您与新人对话时，就会形成链接，并且此后您进行的每一次对话都会加强该链接。

paragraphs.sourceText: You meet new people every day: the grocery worker, the cab driver, new people at work or the security guard at the door. Simply starting a conversation with them will form a link.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您每天都会遇到新朋友：杂货店工人、出租车司机、工作中的新人或门口的保安。只需与他们开始对话即可形成联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: Here are five simple ways that you can make the first move and start a conversation with strangers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您可以通过以下五种简单方法迈出第一步并与陌生人开始对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Suppose you are in a room with someone you don’t know and something within you says “I want to talk with this person” — this is something that mostly happens with all of us. You wanted to say something — the first word — but it just won’t come out, it feels like it is stuck somewhere. I know the feeling and here is my advice: just get it out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 假设你和一个不认识的人在一个房间里，你内心深处有某种东西说“我想和这个人谈谈”——这是我们所有人身上最常发生的事情。你想说些什么——第一个词——但就是说不出来，感觉就像卡在某个地方。我知道这种感觉，这是我的建议：把它说出来。

paragraphs.sourceText: Just think: what is the worst that could happen? They won’t talk with you? Well, they are not talking with you now!
paragraphs.translationZh: 试想一下：可能发生的最坏情况是什么？他们不会和你说话吗？好吧，他们现在不跟你说话！

paragraphs.sourceText: I truly believe that once you get that first word out everything else will just flow. So keep it simple: “Hi”, “Hey” or “Hello” — do the best you can to gather all of the enthusiasm and energy you can, put on a big smile and say “Hi”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我坚信，一旦你说出第一个字，其他一切都会水到渠成。因此，保持简单：“嗨”、“嘿”或“你好”——尽你所能，聚集所有的热情和能量，露出灿烂的微笑，说“嗨”。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s a problem all of us face; you have limited time with the person that you want to talk with and you want to make this talk memorable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这是我们所有人都会面临的问题；您与想要交谈的人相处的时间有限，并且您想让这次谈话令人难忘。

paragraphs.sourceText: Honestly, if we got stuck in the rut of “hi”, “hello”, “how are you?” and “what’s going on?”, you will fail to give the initial jolt to the conversation that can make it so memorable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 老实说，如果我们陷入“嗨”、“你好”、“你好吗？”的套路中。和“发生了什么事？”，你将无法给谈话带来最初的震动，从而使谈话变得如此令人难忘。

paragraphs.sourceText: So don’t be afraid to ask more personal questions. Trust me, you’ll be surprised to see how much people are willing to share if you just ask.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，不要害怕提出更多个人问题。相信我，只要你开口询问，你就会惊讶地发现有多少人愿意分享。

paragraphs.sourceText: When you meet a person for the first time, make an effort to find the things which you and that person have in common so that you can build the conversation from that point. When you start conversation from there and then move outwards, you’ll find all of a sudden that the conversation becomes a lot easier.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当你第一次见到一个人时，努力找到你和那个人的共同点，这样你们就可以从那时开始建立对话。当你从那里开始谈话，然后向外移动时，你会突然发现谈话变得容易多了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Imagine you are pouring your heart out to someone and they are just busy on their phone, and if you ask for their attention you get the response “I can multitask.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 想象一下，你正在向某人倾诉心声，而他们正忙着打电话，如果你请求他们的关注，你会得到这样的答复：“我可以同时处理多项任务。”

paragraphs.sourceText: So when someone tries to communicate with you, just be in that communication wholeheartedly. Make eye contact. Trust me, eye contact is where all the magic happens. When you make eye contact, you can feel the conversation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，当有人试图与您交流时，请全心全意地进行交流。进行目光接触。相信我，眼神交流是所有魔法发生的地方。当你们进行眼神交流时，你可以感觉到谈话。

paragraphs.sourceText: You all came into a conversation where you first met the person, but after some time you may have met again and have forgotten their name. Isn’t that awkward!
paragraphs.translationZh: 你们都在第一次见到这个人的地方进行了一次对话，但一段时间后，你们可能再次见面并忘记了他们的名字。这不是很尴尬吗！

paragraphs.sourceText: So, remember the little details of the people you met or you talked with; perhaps the places they have been to, the places they want to go, the things they like, the things they hate — whatever you talk about.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，请记住您遇到的人或与您交谈过的人的小细节；也许是他们去过的地方、他们想去的地方、他们喜欢的事情、他们讨厌的事情——无论你谈论什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: When you remember such things you can automatically become investor in their wellbeing. So they feel a responsibility to you to keep that relationship going.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当你记住这些事情时，你就会自动成为他们福祉的投资者。所以他们觉得你有责任维持这种关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: That’s it. Five amazing ways that you can make conversation with almost anyone. Every person is a really good book to read, or to have a conversation with!
paragraphs.translationZh: 就是这样。您可以通过五种神奇的方式与几乎任何人进行对话。每个人都是一本值得阅读或交谈的好书！

paragraphs.sourceText: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 将下列文字翻译成中文。将您的翻译写在答题卡上。 （15分）

paragraphs.sourceText: A fifth grader gets a homework assignment to select his future career path from a list of occupations. He ticks “astronaut” but quickly adds “scientist” to the list and selects it as well. The boy is convinced that if he reads enough, he can explore as many career paths as he likes. And so he reads — everything from encyclopedias to science fiction novels. He reads so passionately that his parents have to institute a “no reading policy” at the dinner table.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一名五年级学生接到一份家庭作业，要求从职业列表中选择他未来的职业道路。他勾选了“宇航员”，但很快将“科学家”添加到列表中并选择了它。这个男孩坚信，如果他读得足够多，他可以探索尽可能多的职业道路。所以他读书——从百科全书到科幻小说。他读书如此热情，以至于他的父母不得不在餐桌上制定“不读书政策”。

paragraphs.sourceText: That boy was Bill Gates, and he hasn’t stopped reading yet — not even after becoming one of the most successful people on the planet. Nowadays, his reading material has changed from science fiction and reference books: recently, he revealed that he reads at least 50 nonfiction books a year. Gates chooses nonfiction titles because they explain how the world works. “Each book opens up new avenues of knowledge to explore,” Gates says.
paragraphs.translationZh: 那个男孩就是比尔·盖茨，他还没有停止读书——即使在成为地球上最成功的人之一之后也是如此。如今，他的阅读材料已经从科幻小说和参考书发生了变化：最近，他透露自己每年至少读50本非小说类书籍。盖茨选择非小说类书籍是因为它们解释了世界是如何运作的。 “每本书都开辟了新的知识探索途径，”盖茨说。
